result.title: Protecting Safety during Reasoning Training with Low-Rank Fisher Regularisation
result.summary: Large language models are trained to have safety guardrails, but these can be compromised while fine-tuning for new capabilities, such as reasoning. One way to mitigate this degradation is to modify the fine-tuning objective to preserve safety behaviour, but doing so effectively and efficiently remains challenging. We revisit Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), which penalises parameter updates based on sensitivity estimates from the diagonal of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). While EWC provides some protection, the diagonal approximation ignores interactions between parameters. We address this limitation by exploiting recent findings that safety-relevant behaviour is located in a low-rank subspace within models. Our method, Subspace-Projected Elastic Weight Consolidation (SP-EWC), projects gradients onto this subspace to capture non-diagonal curvature efficiently. We investigate three different ways of identifying the safety subspace: through safety fine-tuning updates (LoRA), safety-related activations (ActSVD), and contrastive representations of safety and utility data (cPCA). We find that this choice substantially affects performance, with SP-EWC using cPCA comparing favourably against existing methods by better maintaining safety guardrails without introducing excessive over-refusal.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对推理能力微调时安全护栏退化的问题，重新审视 EWC 的对角 Fisher 近似局限，提出 SP-EWC：将梯度投影到安全相关的低秩子空间以高效捕捉非对角曲率，并比较通过 LoRA 微调更新、安全相关激活的 SVD（ActSVD）与安全/效用数据的对比表征（cPCA）三种子空间识别方式。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 ActSVD、cPCA 等低秩子空间识别与投影正则手段，可能可供核查用于定位 VLM 内部承载视觉细节或任务必要信息的方向；但该方法作用于参数更新而非推理期 latent 状态，视觉与 LVR 联系需进一步判断。
